brief.headline: Cut dextrose price by 13.6% to match Sayaji's ₹66.48/KG and lock in faster payment terms on their growth run

priceAsk.basis: We already pay Sayaji Industries Limited ₹66.48/KG for the same dextrose. Market asks for Anhydrous Dextrose IP sit in the ₹60–81/kg band, typically ₹66–73/kg, so ₹66.48 is fair and proven. India export price is even lower at 42.95 ₹/kg. No reason to pay 13.6% more here.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to immediate payment (or 15 days) in exchange for a further small price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying at 30 days instead of on delivery frees up ₹4.90 L of our cash; moving to 15 extra days would free another ₹2.45 L — but we flip this: we offer to pay sooner if they sweeten the price, since they're growing fast (21.4%/yr) and will value the cash

brief.financialLeverage: They're financially solid — ₹514.62 Cr revenue, keeping about ₹3.70 of every ₹100 they sell (3.7%), and growing sales by 21.4% a year. But we're tiny to them: our ₹59.65 L is just 0.12% of their business, so on our own we have almost no pull. The play is to bundle a volume commitment or a longer contract, and to make it clear we're lining up Gulshan Polyols or Sanstar as second sources — both are listed, profitable dextrose makers who can match the spec. Because Universal is chasing growth, a credible threat to split the business will get their attention even though we're small today.

evidence.point: We pay 13.6% more than our best dextrose price
evidence.figure: Gap vs best: 13.6%; extra cost ₹14.26 L/yr

evidence.point: Sayaji gives us dextrose at ₹66.48/KG — proven alternative
evidence.figure: Best price we pay: ₹66.48/KG (Sayaji Industries Limited)

evidence.point: Market ask for Anhydrous Dextrose IP is ₹60–81/kg, typically ₹66–73/kg
evidence.figure: Market ask band ₹60–81/kg; verdict MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)

evidence.point: They're growing revenue fast and will want to protect volume
We're a very small customer — only 0.12% of their sales
evidence.figure: Our spend ₹59.65 L vs their revenue ₹514.62 Cr = 0.12%

evidence.point: They keep a slim profit — about ₹3.70 per ₹100 sold

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed ₹2359.06 Cr starch & polyol maker, health score B (62/100) — established dextrose supplier, drop-in alternate to Sayaji; strong capacity and financials

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (₹821.13 Cr), health C (53/100) — growing dextrose capacity, good second-source candidate

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore wet-miller (₹365.39 Cr) making Dextrose ANHYDROUS IV-fluid grade — exact form match; must confirm IP monograph CoA before switching; note weaker health score D (27/100)

risks: We're only 0.12% of their ₹514.62 Cr revenue, so they may ignore a standalone ask — bundle volume or a multi-year commit to get leverage
Their 3.7% profit margin is thin; pushing too hard without offering volume or faster payment may get a flat no
Sayaji at ₹66.48/KG proves the price is real, but Universal may argue location, lead-time or service differences — prepare to audit true all-in cost
None of our current alternates are yet qualified on paper (CoA, audit) — start that process now so the threat of a second source is credible in 60 days
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to grow our dextrose volume with you, but right now we're paying ₹75.51 when Sayaji gives us the same material at ₹66.48 — let's close that gap and talk about a longer commit in return.
